190510101.text: Hello, Traveler. I am Yinxing, The Crux's surgeon at sea.

190510102.text: Whenever a sailor has a health problem, they come to me. I deal with it all — from seasickness and common colds, to amputations, and everything in between.

190510103.text: I'd like to learn about treating injuries and illnesses at sea.

190510104.text: Oh, I presume the Captain arranged this, correct? Alright then, let's begin.

190510105.text: First of all, let me ask you this. What do you think is the biggest danger that all new crew members face?

190510109.text: That can certainly be a problem at sea, but it's not the biggest danger. The most dangerous thing for a newcomer is to underestimate the dangers of life at sea.

190510110.text: I have seen many new crew members who see themselves as young and fighting fit and have no regard for safety. They think that since they are tough enough to look after themselves on land, they'll be fine at sea as well.

190510111.text: Those are the ones that always end up in the sick bay. Everyone should know that being a sailor, especially on a long voyage, is a brutal job in an unforgiving environment.

190510112.text: We have to face malnutrition when we're short on supplies, all kinds of injuries and diseases that the harsh ocean weather can bring...

190510113.text: ...and even the psychological problems that can arise due to isolation and the lack of entertainment.

190510114.text: To make things worse, the lack of medication and treatment options at sea can result in even minor health problems becoming serious, or even fatal...

190510116.text: Haha, you probably thought I was joking, right? That's not surprising. Most newcomers think the same way.

190510117.text: But hopefully you now realize that with a little extra precaution, a lot of these things can be avoided...

190510118.text: Well, I think that's enough for you to think over for now.

190510119.text: Is there anything else you would like to know?

190510202.text: We were so caught up on getting you to join the fleet that we didn't notice we were going a little overboard... Good thing the Captain stepped in.

190510203.text: It's okay. I was hoping to learn a little more about cartography.

190510204.text: Oh! Well, in that case, you have come to the right person. I'm not just blowing smoke, you're looking at the most talented navigator in Liyue Harbor.

190510205.text: I'll start by introducing some chart-reading essentials for new sailors. Feel free to interrupt if you have any questions.

190510206.text: Let's start with what to look for when you get a set of complicated charts.

190510207.text: First, you should always look at any indicated shorelines, islands or reefs, water depths, hydrological conditions, and other hazards.

190510208.text: With these features in mind, you can answer the basic question of "can I chart a safe course through this area."

190510209.text: Visually, nautical charts are a little unique. Unlike land maps, most charts do not have a fixed scale, which means that it can be hard to precisely determine the exact distance between two points.

190510210.text: The most advanced nautical charts come with a supplementary chart, which has different colored lines marked on it to indicate distances.

190510211.text: It's worth mentioning that under my direction, The Crux is using these advanced kinds of charts!

190510212.text: Some cartographers mark out other points of interest on their charts, usually with their own special symbols. If they don't leave any accompanying notes, they can be very difficult to interpret.

190510213.text: For example, charts inherited from the previous navigator?

190510214.text: Haha, not only those. We have tattered and torn charts that we've picked up from all over the place.

190510215.text: To be honest, it can be quite a challenge, even for me. Some of these charts are really old and have symbols that I have never seen before...

190510216.text: But if we don't decipher them, we will certainly miss many secrets of the sea.

190510217.text: Fortunately, we have the Captain with us. She managed to find some ancient books on semiotics that I can use to study the charts further.

190510218.text: I don't think anyone other than our Captain could manage to get these kinds of resources. Old charts and ancient books on semiotics are not the kinds of things that are sold in your average marketplace...

190510219.text: Oops! I've gotten off-topic, hehe. Well, that just about covers the basics of chart-reading.

190510220.text: Is there anything else you would like to know, Traveler?

190510222.text: Drafting charts? That's certainly a more advanced topic. To be honest, I've only attained a smattering of knowledge in that area.

190510223.text: The charts we are using now are just revised versions of the ones left by the previous navigator.

190510224.text: So my mapping experiences have been primarily limited to updating our charts to reflect changes in the sea.

190510225.text: I think you can ask Captain Beidou more about cartography.

190510226.text: One time, the fleet sailed into an uncharted area by mistake. It wasn't long before we turned the fleet around and returned the way we came out for fear of potential hazards.

190510227.text: But Captain Beidou still managed to draft a simple chart of the area we sailed through for if and when we explore the area again.

190510228.text: Incredible, isn't it? I was amazed to see that the Captain could even do cartography.

190510229.text: Then why does she need you as a navigator?

190510230.text: Because I have the talent, and she doesn't want to let it go to waste. Hehe. She treats the whole crew that way.

190510231.text: I initially had the same question myself. After all, in many fleets the captain also works as the navigator. I couldn't understand her reasoning at the time, so I asked her.

190510232.text: She just laughed and told me to wise up, saying that even Rex Lapis never fights alone.

190510233.text: She wants everyone onboard to master their role, so that The Crux is not floating on her alone.

190510234.text: That way, if the day ever comes when she's no longer with the fleet, we will still be able to sail onward without her.

190510235.text: Captain Beidou may seem aloof and even act careless sometimes, but the truth is that she's very considerate of everyone onboard.

190510237.text: My pleasure. A friend of Captain Beidou is a friend of mine!

subQuests.subQuestName: Learn a thing or two from Xu Liushi

190510301.text: Hello, Traveler. Are you here to learn about marine meteorology?

190510303.text: Haha, in my line of work, I've got to have a pair of sharp eyes.

190510304.text: I saw the captain showing you around the training grounds, and then you went to see Yinxing and Huixing.

190510305.text: So, I figured that she probably wants you to get to know the life of a crew member.

190510308.text: Hehe! Okay, let's get started. First, I'll introduce you to the basics of meteorology.

190510309.text: Marine meteorology basically means keeping tabs on the weather as well as other ocean phenomena, so things like sea fog, storm surges, waterspouts, and so on...

190510310.text: These are all potential threats to safe navigation. Luckily, whatever weather might be coming up, there's always some kind of sign that gives it away in advance.

190510311.text: Take waterspouts for example. They're caused by high-speed rotating winds on the surface of the ocean. They can engulf large ships and do immense damage.

190510312.text: But, if you know that waterspouts can only form in an environment with high temperature, high humidity, and large clouds, then you can be well-prepared.

190510313.text: You will be even more alert if you also know that the presence of winds blowing in opposite directions with a significant difference in speed is a direct precursor to the formation of waterspouts.

190510314.text: And most importantly, if you spot a small white vortex emerging from the clouds, you should immediately notify the crew to steer clear of what's ahead.

190510315.text: So there you go, those are the warning signs of waterspouts. I am proud to say that, over the years, I haven't let a single one sneak up on my watch.

subQuests.subQuestName: Head to the fishing village near Wangshu Inn
Take a stroll with Beidou in the fishing village
Go with Beidou to the fishing village for a walk

190515201.text: I can't wait to see how you perform.

190515301.text: Be sure to take good care of yourself.

190515401.text: One day, I will decipher all these symbols.

190515501.text: Find me anytime if you want to know more.

190519901.text: People used to call this place "Downriver," because the villagers apparently moved here from a place called "Upriver."

190519902.text: With them, they brought their knowledge of fishing which had been passed down from generation to generation. I learned a lot from them when I was here.

190519903.text: Now, Upriver is long gone and Downriver is all but deserted. It won't be long before no one even remembers what these places are called.

190519904.text: About a year or two after I arrived, the village chief fell ill during the winter and passed away.

190519905.text: During that same period, the harvest was getting worse and the fishermen's catch was getting smaller day by day.

190519906.text: Without the village chief to handle the situation, people began blaming each other. There were even rumors that some families had been overfishing, leaving nothing for the rest of the village to catch.

190519907.text: But in the end, they all turned on me, saying that they shouldn't have ever taken me in. They said I was bad luck.

190519908.text: They pointed to how that dog died on the first day I arrived.

190519909.text: Next thing you know, the village chief dies, then all the fish die out.

190519910.text: They said I was a living curse, and the downfall of the village was all my fault.

190519911.text: I told them that I didn't understand. I'm not a curse, I'm just Beidou.

190519912.text: Then some of the villagers started shouting and drove me out of the village.

190519913.text: They shouted, "Nandou controls life! Beidou controls death... Beidou controls death!"

190519914.text: Before then, all I knew about my name was that it had something to do with the stars.

190519915.text: It wasn't until then that I realized that Beidou was a constellation, and the Alcor, one of its stars, was an omen of death.
